mechanism_claims.claim_text: Temporin B and temporin B L1FK directly induce membrane conductance/defect-like activity in model DPhPE/DPhPG and DPhPG membranes, with temporin B L1FK active at lower concentration than temporin B in both membrane systems.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Temporin B and temporin B L1FK

source_locator.section_locator: xml:sec=20:Membrane activity of temporin B peptides

mechanism_claims.limitations: Model membranes are mechanistic surrogates; the result supports membrane activity mechanism, not a quantified bacterial-killing time course.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Temporin B KKG6A retains antibacterial activity for selected Gram-negative targets but requires much higher peptide concentrations for detectable model-membrane conductance and is ineffective against Gram-positive isolates in Table 2.

source_locator.section_locator: xml:sec=13:Primary sequence and antibacterial activity; xml:sec=20:Membrane activity of temporin B peptides

mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanistic conclusion is bounded to model membrane conductance and source-reviewed MIC selectivity; no host toxicity row is extracted from this primary paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper interprets L1FK improvement as associated with increased membrane insertion/reduced self-association, while KKG6A is framed as a different membrane-interaction mode involving headgroup-region interaction and lipid-domain disruption rather than readily detectable channel conductance.
